record.title: Microduck head speaker — a 35 x 25 x 7 mm box speaker (Pollen's placeholder mesh); exact part CANNOT DETERMINE; representative: '3525' 8 Ω 2 W cavity speaker
record.why: THE EXACT PART IS NOT IN ANY SOURCE. Pollen's MJCF carries a 12-triangle placeholder box 35.0 x 25.0 x 7.0 mm named `speaker` in the head (docs/PARTS.md row 38); the runtime only says the codec is a TLV320AIC3104 at I2C 0x18 driving ALSA `plughw:aic3104`, and the community teardown says 'line out' — driver and impedance are CANNOT DETERMINE (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §7); the AMPLIFIER question was closed 2026-09-02 — see record.drive_path_resolved: the codec's recommended minimum load is 16 ohm and its maximum output 30 mW into 16 ohm (SLAS510G p.7, p.11), so an 8 ohm 2 W transducer needs an amplifier, and the teardown's 'line out' (10 kohm recommended load) is an amplifier input. WHAT THIS FOLDER CARRIES INSTEAD, said plainly: a REPRESENTATIVE. The '3525' cavity speaker is a commodity 35 x 25 mm 8 Ω 2 W box speaker whose envelope (35 x 25 x 6.8 mm) matches Pollen's placeholder to within 0.2 mm in height and exactly in plan. Its figures come from a reseller's spec table (ABRA Electronics SPK-3525-2W-GH, fetched 2026-09-02, docs/, sha256 in PROVENANCE.json) because NO MANUFACTURER PUBLISHES A DATASHEET FOR IT — the maker is anonymous. For contrast the nearest part WITH a manufacturer datasheet, Same Sky (CUI) CMS-35208N, is 35.5 x 20.5 x 8.0 mm (read off its rendered p.1) and DISCONTINUED — the wrong width. WHAT SETTLES IT: a teardown photo of the head, or Pollen naming the part.
record.subsector_why: SCHEMA.md's closed sector list has no audio/transducer value; a loudspeaker converts electrical drive into mechanical motion, which is the closest fit ('actuator'). The atech speaker module on the workshop shelf is sector atech_module, which does not apply here. Stated so the choice is visible.
record.lifecycle_why: anonymous commodity part; ABRA showed 'Availability: In stock' on 2026-09-02, a stock state, not a lifecycle.
record.origin_why: the figures were read off a FETCHED reseller page (ABRA Electronics) that reproduces the maker's spec table verbatim, plus a second reseller page (thingbits.net, XHXDZ-3525-8R2W) and Same Sky's own CMS-35208N PDF for the contrast part — all saved under docs/ with sha256 in PROVENANCE.json. Not 'measured': no speaker has been on a bench here. Not 'standard': none applies. THE HONEST CAVEAT: for the 3525 the 'vendor' is a reseller, because the manufacturer is not named anywhere.

drive_path_resolved.$about: Closing half of 'driver, impedance and whether the codec's own output or an external amplifier drives it are all CANNOT DETERMINE' — the amplifier half is now answered from TI's own numbers. Lane C, 2026-09-02.
drive_path_resolved.verdict: AN AMPLIFIER IS REQUIRED. The TLV320AIC3104 cannot drive a 3525-class 8 ohm 2 W speaker, on the load resistance alone.
the_numbers_verbatim: SLAS510G §8.3 Recommended Operating Conditions, p.7: 'Stereo headphone output load resistance | 16 | Ω' and 'Stereo line output load resistance | 10 | kΩ'.
SLAS510G §8 Electrical Characteristics, p.11: 'PO Maximum output power | RL = 32 Ω | 15 | mW' and 'RL = 16 Ω | 30 | mW'.

SLAS510G §10 p.39: 'output drivers are individually capable of driving 30 mW each into a 16-Ω load in single-ended configuration, and they can be used in pairs connected in bridge-terminated load (BTL) configuration between two driver outputs.'
drive_path_resolved.the_arithmetic: The representative transducer is 8 ohm / 2 W (ABRA SPK-3525-2W-GH). 8 ohm is BELOW the codec's recommended minimum load of 16 ohm, so direct drive is out of the recommended operating conditions before any power question is asked. And 30 mW into 16 ohm is 1.5 % of 2 W; even reading the BTL note at its most generous (two drivers in bridge = 4x the single-ended power into the same load) gives 120 mW, 6 % of 2 W. In dB, 30 mW is 10*log10(0.030) = -15.2 dB relative to the 1 W at which any speaker's sensitivity is quoted; the fitted speaker's sensitivity is not published, so the resulting SPL is not stated here.
drive_path_resolved.and_the_teardown_agrees: The community teardown reports the output routing as 'line out, volume 9/9' (research/raw/community/replica_hardware-teardown.en.md:325). The codec's line outputs are LEFT_LOP/LOM and RIGHT_LOP/LOM (pins 27-30, SLAS510G Table 7-1 p.5), whose recommended load is 10 kOHM — an amplifier's input impedance, not a loudspeaker's.
drive_path_resolved.lineage_agrees_too: Open Duck Mini v2's BOM carries a separate 'Amplifier' line at EUR 5 beside its 'Speaker' line at EUR 6 (research/open_duck_mini_v2_bom.csv, 'Expression package'). The family has always put an amplifier between the codec and the transducer.
still_cannot_determine: WHICH amplifier, and where it sits — on the Robot HAT, on a separate module, or built into the speaker assembly. Pollen publishes no HAT schematic. A class-D mono amp of the MAX98357A/PAM8302 class is what the community teardown suggests substituting (replica_hardware-teardown.en.md:389, 'a MAX98357A amplifier if you give up recording'), which is a recommendation for a rebuild, not an observation of the original.

THE FITTED TRANSDUCER's impedance and power. If it were a >=16 ohm capsule run at tens of milliwatts, HPLOUT/HPROUT could drive it directly and in spec — the codec's headphone outputs exist for exactly that. This verdict is therefore conditional on the 8 ohm 2 W representative, and says so.
The single figure that would settle both at once: an ohmmeter across the speaker's own leads on a production robot.
drive_path_resolved.consequence_for_the_hat_design: electronics/robot-hat/ must carry an amplifier stage between the codec's output and the speaker connector, with its own supply decoupling, or the board will not make sound. That is a schematic block the PCB lane cannot omit and cannot copy from anywhere — nobody has published it.
